extracted.subtask_description: Practical rules and precautions for drawing, remitting, converting, and collecting bills of exchange and for converting/valuing different coinages across cities (Venice, London, Bruges, Bologna, etc.). Includes advice on protests, fraud prevention, and arithmetic/conversion procedures between denominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and identification of 'cambio reale' (real exchange)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish the 'cambio reale' as that exchange which is truly received — i.e., the money actually obtained at the place of payment (what 'veramente si chiama reale').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute coin values and bills according to what is actually received locally; avoid treating as real any bill or change that is only nominal or fictitious. The text repeatedly contrasts apparent values and the 'reale' value received in hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify place and tenor (term) of payment on a bill of exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter/tratta (Ira de cambio) must specify the city (e.g. Venezia, Londra, Bruggia, Anversa) and the payment term so payment is made 'secondo il suo tenore e termine'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting a bill name the city of payment and the exact tenor/term; payments are made according to the tenor and local custom of the named place. If ambiguous, disputes and non-payment may arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute coin values by local tariff at place of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Monete (coins) are to be computed 'in suo luogo' using the tariff/custom of the place where payment occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting one coin to another, use the usual local tariff (tariffa al suo luogo) rather than the drawer's local reckoning. The text gives many numeric examples and local equivalences (ducati, groffi, fiorini, popolini, etc.) to be used as reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of letters of exchange and remittance practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters (lettera della tratta) and remittances may be sent to have funds collected by a friend or correspondent; such instruments transfer the right to collect sums at distant markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep clear records of to whom letters (or remittances) were delivered and ensure the correspondent's name and reputation are known. A letter received entitles the bearer to demand the stated payment in that market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests, demands, and documentation when payment is refused
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bill is not paid, the drawer/holder must make demand and, if necessary, protest the non-payment; these actions document the failure and may preserve remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make timely demand/protest; retain copies/letters as evidence. The text stresses making 'domanda' and protest so non-payment cannot be pleaded later, and that failure to protest may prejudice recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precautions against fictitious bills and fraud ('cambio fittido')
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid relying on fictitious exchange or on names/letters of unknown or dishonest correspondents; fictitious bills cause loss and are actionable risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the names of exchangers and traders; do not accept or issue bills through dubious intermediaries. The text advises caution ('cautela') and to know 'nomi de' cambi' reputable among merchants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer few, reliable intermediaries — avoid excessive intermediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not involve unnecessarily many third parties in an exchange chain; multiple intermediaries increase complexity and risk of non-payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible use a direct trustworthy correspondent; the text warns that adding many hands ('intrigare cu altri corri') complicates tracing and recovery and may produce disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion procedure and equivalence tables between coin denominations and cities
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert currency amounts according to established equivalences and examples (ducato ↔ groffi ↔ fiorino ↔ popolino, etc.), and relative values that differ by city and by commodity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local equivalence tables and compute by multiplication/division as illustrated in the numerous worked examples. The manuscript lists many concrete equivalences (e.g., valuations of ducati, groffi, populationi, various city-specific rates) to guide conversion calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to ask for and record local exchange value ('quante mene donerà dare')
rubrics_metrics.description: When obtaining a local rate, explicitly ask a local changer/merchant how many of their local coins correspond to one unit of the foreign coin, and record the returned proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase the question to the local changer and transcribe the local response; the text suggests concrete wording and examples for querying the amount of local coins given per unit foreign coin, then using that rate in calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for splitting large sums and staged payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Large sums may be broken into portions (fractions) to be converted or remitted in stages, following rules about timing and rounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual gives procedures for splitting sums into parts (e.g., by hundreds, thousands, etc.) and converting each part in turn; it shows how to carry remainders and how staged receipts affect accounting and timing of collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fractional accounting and rounding conventions in exchange arithmetic
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting between units use consistent rules for fractions, carry-overs, and rounding to the smallest local units (picioli, denari, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text contains detailed arithmetic examples showing how to break down amounts into subunits and how to convert and round; follow those conventions to avoid small discrepancies that can accumulate into loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of goods and commodities when expressed in local currency
rubrics_metrics.description: When bills concern proceeds from goods (grain, wine, etc.), value the commodity in the currency of the place where it will be sold/paid, using local measures and prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript gives examples (wheat, grain, etc.) and shows that the local market price/quality affects the conversion and should be taken into account when specifying amounts on a bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep knowledge of the reputation and lists of reliable 'cambi' (exchangers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and consult a list of known reputable exchangers and their usual practices; this knowledge reduces the risk of accepting bad bills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text advises to be aware 'di nomi de' cambi' present among merchants, and to rely on those with established good repute; also to be wary of those known for fraud or unreliable practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of returns, counter-trades, and remittances when an intermediary fails
rubrics_metrics.description: If an intermediary fails to remit or pay, trace back through the chain, use letters/protests, and apply local remedies; differentiate between genuine inability and fraudulent refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual discusses situations where a merchant in one city sends a bill via another and that intermediate merchant fails; it recommends documentary protest, contacting other market participants, and using the documented chain to establish claims.
